score_change_reason: Quant and risk-manager evidence weakens direct transfer of L-161 hard-fail to H_1692 (M07 quality and scaling are cleaner), so I raise by 1 point; however PIT, IC-to-return transmission, and tail/cost risks still prevent a high score.

agreements.point: Agreed that S1 must explicitly compare H_1692 residual ICIR vs M07 standalone and log monthly M07-M18 correlation/beta_t; this directly tests whether residualization adds independent alpha or is just relabeled M07.
Agreed that crisis-conditional tail dependence and beta-linked drawdown risk can dominate average IC, so S3 TDC and tail-risk suite are mandatory before any confident admission.

rebuttals.point: Disagree with treating projected LOO SR uplift and role-honesty as near-established pre-S1/S3; those are expectation-level estimates and can reverse once real KR costs, crisis co-movement, and coupling diagnostics are measured.

Disagree that strong foundational literature justifies a high practical score here, because the exact residualization mechanism lacks direct peer-reviewed precedent and citation integrity issues were still unresolved.

strongest_opposing_argument: The quant argument that L-161 hard-fail was mainly M01(sd distortion) specific and not directly portable to M07(sd=1.0, long sample, positive recent ICIR) is the strongest challenge to my original family-overlap rejection logic.
kill_scenarios_update: New kill scenario: expanding-window beta_t can converge toward quasi-constant across structural breaks, making residual ranks >0.95 correlated with M07 standalone; if combined with sector concentration spikes (high HHI), momentum-crash tail losses can occur despite positive in-sample IC.
